summary: Sequoia NP lookout: a 1964 steel cab replaced a 1927 wood tower; last staffed 1996; the 2021 Paradise Fire damaged it, and sources disagree on what survived.

corrections.why: The Paradise Fire of September 2021 damaged the lookout, and the registers say it was reported lost. NHLR says it was damaged with its condition still being evaluated; FFLOS says it was reported lost and overrun; Peakbagging says the main building survived. No source says it stood unharmed.

resolved_conflicts.field: fate of the cabin after the 2021 Paradise Fire
resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the lookout and communications infrastructure were damaged, with the structure's condition still being evaluated in October 2021. FFLOS says it was reported lost and overrun. Peakbagging says the main building survived and only an aluminum equipment shelter burned. The story reports all three without choosing one.

sources.title: Milk Ranch Peak, Tulare County, California

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'standing' status is not supported: the register accounts and Peakbagging conflict on the fire damage, and none describes it as unharmed. Sources disagree on whether the main building survived; a USFS or NPS statement from the October 2021 access would settle it. The Sequoia NF Facebook post returned no text when read, so it is not cited. No source after 2021 on rebuild, access or rental. The Peakbagging page is undated. Used 6 page reads and 1 search. Staffing as_of is the 2021 fire year, since the 1996 date is the last staffing and the Peakbagging 'not currently staffed' note is undated.
